title: Electrical Protection and Wire Sizing
markdown:
Instructor Run Sheet - REVISED

PV101 Day 5 - Monday, July 13, 2026

| Day 5 focus | Commissioning, verification, wire protection, voltage drop, and structured troubleshooting using the systems built on Day 4. |
| --- | --- |
| Important change | Do not repeat the small-system build. Preserve the Day 4 builds and use them as live training systems. |

# Learning targets

Explain voltage, current, resistance, and power in practical language.

Calculate watts and current for common 12 V loads.

Identify where fuses belong and explain that they protect conductors.

Commission an existing PV system using visual inspection and meter evidence.

Measure voltage drop without rebuilding the system.

Diagnose safe instructor-created faults using observe, predict, measure, act, verify.

Leave a system labeled and documented for the next technician.

# Materials

Five completed Day 4 training systems. Keep them assembled unless a correction is necessary.

Multimeters, labels/tape, markers, inspection tags, spare fuses, hand tools.

Optional clamp meter and known 12 V loads.

Printed quiz, commissioning sheets, fault cards, and exit tickets.

# Schedule

| Time | Block | Instructor notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 10:00-10:10 | Landing / readiness | Confirm yesterday’s systems are present. No energizing yet. |
| 10:10-10:25 | Morning quiz | Individual. Use results to select review points. |
| 10:25-10:50 | Quiz debrief | Volts, amps, watts, fuse purpose, placement, and voltage drop. |
| 10:50-11:20 | Mini-lesson | Commissioning versus building. A finished system still has to prove itself. |
| 11:20-11:45 | Instructor demonstration | Visual inspection, expected readings, and voltage-drop measurement. |
| 11:45-12:00 | Fault-method briefing | Observe -> predict -> measure -> act -> verify. No random touching. |
| 12:00-12:30 | Lunch / reset | Instructor installs safe faults or prepares fault cards. |
| 12:30-1:15 | Round 1: Commissioning | Teams inspect and document one completed system. |
| 1:15-2:10 | Rounds 2-3: Fault rotation | Teams rotate through safe faults; evidence required before correction. |
| 2:10-2:35 | Wire sizing / voltage-drop application | Use measured or assigned loads to justify conductor and fuse choices. |
| 2:35-3:00 | Teach-back / restore / cleanup | Return every kit to known-good condition and document it. |

# Safe fault menu

Removed or blown fuse.

PV disconnected from controller.

Load disconnected or switched off at an unexpected point.

Loose, unenergized connection identified before power-up.

Incorrect meter setting or lead placement as a demonstration fault.

Mislabeled conductor or missing system label.

High-resistance connection simulated only with an approved training method; do not create heat intentionally.

Controller sequence/state issue that can be corrected without bypassing manufacturer instructions.

# Do not use as live faults

Intentional reverse polarity on energized equipment.

Unfused battery short circuits.

Deliberate overheating, damaged conductors, or exposed live copper.

Any fault that relies on a student “seeing what happens.” We already know what happens.

# Instructor safety holds

No system energizes until visual inspection and polarity check are complete.

Any unexpected heat, smell, spark, unstable reading, or damaged insulation means stop and isolate.

Only one change at a time during troubleshooting.

After each fault, restore the system and independently verify normal readings.

The lab win is a defensible diagnosis, not merely making the inverter turn on.
